en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānuloma (1), Tikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (1) 1.2.
Kusala-ttika (The Triplet of the Wholesome)
Section on Analysis:
Positive (Anuloma) Root Condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of root condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate...
Dependent on three aggregates, [arise] three aggregates; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on a wholesome state, an indeterminate state arises by way of root-condition:
dependent on wholesome aggregates, mind-originated matter arises. Dependent on a wholesome state, both wholesome and indeterminate states arise.
By way of root condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter;
dependent on three aggregates, there arise one aggregate and mind-produced matter; dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of root condition: dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an indeterminate state arises by way of root condition: dependent on unwholesome aggregates...
Matter produced by mind. Dependent on unwholesome states, unwholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of root condition:
dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates and matter produced by mind arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate and matter produced by mind arise; dependent on two aggregates, two [aggregates and matter produced by mind arise].
The aggregates and mind-produced matter.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of root condition:
dependent on one resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise; dependent on three aggregates... [and so forth].
One aggregate and mind-produced matter; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-produced matter;
at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one resultant indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-produced matter;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate and kamma-produced matter; dependent on two aggregates...
Two aggregates and the matter produced by kamma; dependent on the aggregates, the physical basis (vatthu); dependent on the physical basis, the aggregates;

dependent on one great primary element (mahābhūta), three great primary elements; dependent on three great primary elements, one great primary element; dependent on two great primary elements, two great primary elements;
dependent on the great primary elements, mind-originated matter, matter produced by kamma, and derived matter (upādārūpa).

Dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of the root condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great primaries, mind-originated matter [arises].

Dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of the root condition: dependent on unwholesome aggregates and the great primaries, mind-originated matter [arises].
Object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*).

Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of object condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.

Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of object condition: dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of object condition:
dependent on one resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises;
dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one resultant-indeterminate aggregate...
Three aggregates; one aggregate dependent on three aggregates; two aggregates dependent on two aggregates;
aggregates dependent on the basis (vatthu).
Predominance (adhipati).
Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of predominance condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on a wholesome state, an indeterminate state arises by way of predominance condition: [dependent on] wholesome aggregates...
dependent on [the mind], mind-originated matter arises. Dependent on a wholesome state, wholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of predominance condition:
dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate and mind-originated matter arise; dependent on two aggregates...
Two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of predominance condition: dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an indeterminate state arises by way of the predominance condition:
dependent on unwholesome aggregates, mind-produced matter arises. Dependent on an unwholesome state, both unwholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of the predominance condition:
dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Form: dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate and mind-produced matter arise; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of predominance condition: [dependent on] resultant-indeterminate...
Dependent on one functional indeterminate aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter;
dependent on three aggregates, there arises one aggregate and mind-produced matter; dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter;
dependent on one great primary element, there arise three great primary elements; dependent on three great primary elements...

Dependent on one great primary element, two great primary elements [arise]; dependent on two great primary elements, two great primary elements [arise]; dependent on the great primary elements, mind-originated derived matter [arises].

Dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of the predominance condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great primary elements, mind-originated matter [arises].

Dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of the predominance condition: dependent on unwholesome aggregates and the great primary elements, mind-originated matter [arises].
Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*) … by way of contiguity condition (*samanantara-paccaya*):
dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates [arise]. (Proximity and contiguity conditions are similar to the object condition.)
Dependent on a simultaneously arisen wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of simultaneous condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on a wholesome state, an indeterminate state arises by way of co-nascence condition:
dependent on wholesome aggregates, mind-produced matter arises. Dependent on a wholesome state, both wholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of co-nascence condition:
dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Matter: one aggregate dependent on three aggregates and mind-produced matter; two aggregates dependent on two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of conascence condition: [dependent on] one unwholesome aggregate...
Dependent on three aggregates, [arise] three aggregates; dependent on three aggregates, [arises] one aggregate; dependent on two aggregates, [arise] two aggregates.
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an indeterminate state arises by way of co-nascence condition:
dependent on unwholesome aggregates, mind-originated matter [arises]. Dependent on an unwholesome state, both unwholesome and indeterminate states [arise].
They arise by way of the co-nascence condition: dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate and mind-produced matter arise; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-produced matter arise.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of conascence condition:
dependent on one resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate and mind-produced matter arise; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates [and mind-produced matter] arise.
And mind-originated matter: at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one resultant indeterminate aggregate, there are three aggregates and kamma-produced matter;
dependent on three aggregates, there is one aggregate and kamma-produced matter;
dependent on two aggregates, there are two aggregates and kamma-produced matter; dependent on the aggregates, there is the [heart-]base; dependent on the [heart-]base, [the aggregates arise].
The aggregates: dependent on one great primary element, three great primary elements [arise]; dependent on three great primary elements, one great primary element [arises];
dependent on two great primary elements, two great primary elements [arise]; dependent on the great primary elements, mind-originated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter [arise].
Dependent on one external great primary element, three great primary elements [arise]; dependent on three great primary elements...
One great primary element; two great primary elements in dependence on two great primary elements; derived form in dependence on the great primary elements;

nutriment-produced: one great primary element in dependence on three great primary elements, three great primary elements in dependence on one great primary element, two great primary elements in dependence on two great primary elements, and derived form in dependence on the great primary elements; temperature-produced...
Dependent on one great primary element (mahābhūta), three great primary elements arise; dependent on three great primary elements, one great primary element arises;

dependent on two great primary elements, two great primary elements arise; dependent on the great primary elements, derived matter (upādārūpa) arises; and in the case of non-percipient beings, dependent on one great primary element, three great primary elements arise;
dependent on three great primary elements, one great primary element arises; dependent on two great primary elements...
Dependent on two great elements, dependent on the great elements, derived matter consisting of kamma-born matter arises.

Dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of co-nascence condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises.

Dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of co-nascence condition: dependent on unwholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-originated matter arises.

Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of mutuality condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.

Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of mutuality condition: dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of mutuality condition:
dependent on one resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises;
dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise; at the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one resultant-indeterminate aggregate...
Three aggregates and the [heart-]base; one aggregate and the base in dependence on three aggregates;
two aggregates and the base in dependence on two aggregates; the base in dependence on the aggregates; the aggregates in dependence on the base;

and one great primary element in dependence on three great primary elements, three great primary elements in dependence on one great primary element, and two great primary elements in dependence on [the other two].
Two great elements: external ... nutriment-originated ... temperature-originated ...
for non-percipient beings, dependent on one great element, three great elements arise; dependent on three great elements, one great element arises;
dependent on two great elements, two great elements arise.
Dependence:

In dependence upon a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of dependence condition—dependent upon one wholesome aggregate... (The dependence condition is the same as the conascence condition.
Strong-dependence.

Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*): dependent on one wholesome aggregate... (The decisive support condition is similar to the object condition.
Pre-nascence:
Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of pre-nascence condition (*purejāta-paccaya*): dependent on one wholesome aggregate...
Dependent on three aggregates, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
[This is] the basis as a pre-arising condition (*purejātapaccaya*).
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of the pre-arising condition: dependent on one unwholesome aggregate...
Dependent on three aggregates, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
[This is] the basis as a pre-arising condition (*purejāta-paccaya*).
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of pre-arising condition: [namely,] the resultant-indeterminate...
In dependence on one functional-ineffective aggregate, three aggregates [arise]; in dependence on three aggregates, one aggregate;
in dependence on two aggregates, two aggregates. [This occurs] by way of the basis as a pre-arising condition (*purejāta-paccaya*).
Repetition (*āsevana*...).

Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of repetition-condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.

Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of repetition-condition: dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of repetition condition:
dependent on one functional-indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises;
dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
Dependent on wholesome kamma-dhamma, a wholesome dhamma arises by way of kamma-condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate … three.
Dependent on unwholesome dhamma … three.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of kamma-condition:
dependent on one resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregate … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … dependent on one great primary,
the other three great primaries arise … pe … dependent on the great primaries, mind-originated matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter arise.

In the case of non-percipient beings, dependent on one great primary element (mahābhūta), three great primary elements arise … [and so on] … dependent on the great primary elements, kamma-produced derived matter (upādārūpa) arises.

Dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of kamma-condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great primary elements, mind-originated matter arises.

Dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of kamma-condition: dependent on unwholesome aggregates and the great primary elements, mind-originated matter arises.
Dependent on a resultant indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of resultant condition:
dependent on one resultant-indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise; dependent on three aggregates... [and so forth].
One aggregate and mind-produced matter; depending on two aggregates, two aggregates and mind-produced matter [arise];
at the moment of rebirth-linking, depending on one resultant indeterminate aggregate, three aggregates and kamma-produced matter [arise];
depending on three aggregates, one aggregate and kamma-produced matter [arise]; depending on two aggregates...
Two aggregates and the matter produced by them; dependent on the aggregates, the [heart-]base; dependent on the base, the aggregates;
dependent on one great primary, three great primaries; dependent on three great primaries, one great primary; dependent on two great primaries, two great primaries;
and dependent on the great primaries, mind-produced matter, matter produced by kamma, and derived matter.
Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of nutriment condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate ... three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of nutriment condition: dependent on one unwholesome aggregate ... three.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of nutriment-condition:
dependent on one resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregate … pe … at the moment of rebirth-linking … pe … dependent on one great primary,
three great primaries arise … pe … dependent on the great primaries, mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter arise.
Dependent on one great primary derived from nutriment … dependent on great primaries, derived matter [arises].

Dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states … Dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of nutriment condition: mind-produced matter arises dependent on unwholesome aggregates and great primaries.
Dependent on a wholesome state by way of faculty condition, a wholesome state arises: dependent on one wholesome aggregate … three.
Dependent on an unwholesome state … three.
Dependent on an indeterminate state … [and so on] … dependent on one great primary element of non-percipient beings … [and so on]. (The faculty condition is the same as the kamma condition.
Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of jhāna-condition … by way of path-condition. (The jhāna-condition and the path-condition are also the same as the root-condition.)

Dependent on an associated wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of association condition—dependent on one wholesome aggregate, etc. (The association condition is the same as the object condition.
Dissociation...
Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of dissociation condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise;
[and] the physical basis [arises] by way of dissociation condition. Dependent on a wholesome state, an indeterminate state arises by way of dissociation condition: [dependent on] wholesome...
Dependent on the aggregates, mind-originated matter [arises]. [This is] by way of dissociation condition (*vippayuttapaccaya*).
Dependent on a wholesome state, both wholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of dissociation condition:
dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates and mind-originated matter [arise]; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate and mind-originated matter [arise].
Matter: dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
The aggregates are related to the physical basis by dissociation-condition; mind-produced matter is related to the aggregates by dissociation-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by dissociation-condition: one unwholesome...
Dependent on one aggregate, three aggregates arise; dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate arises; dependent on two aggregates, two aggregates arise.
[This is] the basis as a dissociation condition. Dependent on an unwholesome state, a neutral state arises by way of dissociation condition:
dependent on unwholesome aggregates, mind-originated matter arises. [Dependent on] aggregates...
Conditioned by dissociation. Dependent on an unwholesome state, unwholesome and indeterminate states arise by way of dissociation-condition:
dependent on one unwholesome aggregate, three aggregates and mind-produced matter arise;
dependent on three aggregates, one aggregate and mind-produced matter arise; dependent on two aggregates... [and so forth].
Two aggregates and mind-produced matter. The aggregates are related to the [heart-]base by dissociation condition. Mind-produced matter is related to the aggregates by dissociation condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by dissociation condition: [namely,] resultant-indeterminate...
In dependence on one functional-ineffective aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter;
in dependence on three aggregates, there arises one aggregate and mind-produced matter; in dependence on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter.
The aggregates are related to the [heart-]base by dissociation condition. Mind-produced matter...

The aggregates are related to the base by dissociation condition. At the moment of rebirth-linking, dependent on one resultant indeterminate aggregate, there arise three aggregates and kamma-produced matter;
dependent on three aggregates, there arise one aggregate and kamma-produced matter;
dependent on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and kamma-produced matter. The aggregates are related to the base by dissociation condition.

Conditioned by the aggregates, there is resultant-form (kaṭattārūpa) by way of dissociation condition. Dependent on the aggregates, there is the physical basis; dependent on the physical basis, there are the aggregates.
The aggregates are related to the physical basis by way of dissociation condition. The physical basis is related to the aggregates by way of dissociation condition.

Dependent on one great primary element, there are three great primary elements; dependent on three great primary elements, there is one great primary element; dependent on two great primary elements...
Two great elements; dependent on the great elements, mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter [arise].
[This is] dissociation condition for the aggregates.

Dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of dissociation condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-produced matter [arises]. [This is] dissociation condition for the aggregates.

Dependent on unwholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of dissociation condition: dependent on unwholesome aggregates and the great elements, mind-produced matter [arises]. [This is] dissociation condition for the aggregates.
Presence:
Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of presence condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates [arise].

Dependent on a wholesome state that has ceased (*natthi*), a wholesome state arises by way of the cessation condition (*natthi-paccaya*) ... by way of the disappearance condition (*vigata-paccaya*). (The cessation condition and the disappearance condition are similar to the object condition.
Non-disappearance (*avigata*).

Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of non-disappearance condition: dependent on one wholesome aggregate, three aggregates arise. (The non-disappearance condition is the same as the conascence condition.
These twenty-three conditions should be expanded upon by one who is reciting them.
Section on Enumeration.
In the pure cause condition, there are nine; in the object condition, three; in the predominance condition, nine; in the proximity condition, three; in the contiguity condition, three;

in the conascence condition, nine; in the mutuality condition, three; in the support condition, nine; in the decisive support condition, three; in the prenascence condition, three; in the repetition condition, three.
With respect to kamma: nine; with respect to resultant: one; with respect to nutriment: nine; with respect to faculty: nine; with respect to jhāna: nine; with respect to path: nine;

with respect to association: three; with respect to dissociation: nine; with respect to presence: nine; with respect to absence: three; with respect to disappearance: three; with respect to non-disappearance: nine. This is the enumeration based on the root of cause.

In the Duka [classification], with root condition (hetu-paccaya): three in the object (ārammaṇa), nine in the predominance (adhipati), three in the immediate (anantara), three in the contiguity (samanantara),

nine in the conascence (sahajāta), three in the mutuality (aññamañña), nine in the support (nissaya), three in the decisive support (upanissaya), three in the prenascence (purejāta), and three in the repetition (āsevana).
In the kamma condition, nine; in the resultant condition, one; in the nutriment condition, nine; in the faculty condition, nine; in the jhāna condition, nine; in the path condition, nine;

in the association condition, three; in the dissociation condition, nine; in the presence condition, nine; in the absence condition, three; in the disappearance condition, three; in the non-disappearance condition, nine. (Triplet)
With root condition, object condition, and predominance condition: three; with proximity: three; with contiguity:
three; with conascence: three; with mutuality: three; with dependence: three; with strong-dependence: three; with prenascence: three; with repetition: three; with kamma: three;
with resultant: one; with nutriment: three; with faculty: three; with jhāna: three; with path: three; with association: [three].
Three [factors] by way of dissociation, three by way of presence, three by way of absence, three by way of disappearance, and three by way of non-disappearance …pe….
The twelvefold [combination]:
by way of root-condition, object-condition, predominance-condition, proximity-condition, contiguity-condition, and conascence-condition.
With mutual condition, support condition, decisive support condition, prenascence condition, and repetition condition:
three for kamma, three for nutriment, three for faculty, three for jhāna, three for path,
three for association, three for dissociation, three for presence, three for absence, three for disappearance, and three for non-disappearance …pe….
Twenty-two [factors] by way of root-condition, object-condition … pe … repetition-condition, kamma-condition, nutriment-condition,
faculty-condition, jhāna-condition, path-condition, association-condition, dissociation-condition, presence-condition, and absence-condition.
With the disappearance condition, there are three [answers] for the non-disappearance [condition] …pe….
Thirteenfold:
with the root condition, the object condition …pe… the prenascence condition, the kamma condition, the resultant condition, and the nutriment condition.
One [condition] in the case of the faculties, one in the case of the jhānas, one in the case of the path, one in the case of association, one in the case of dissociation,
one in the case of presence, one in the case of absence, one in the case of disappearance, and one in the case of non-disappearance …pe… (The twenty-two-fold combination).
With root condition, object condition …pe… prenascence condition, kamma condition, resultant condition,
nutriment condition, faculty condition, jhāna condition, path condition, association condition, dissociation condition,
presence condition, absence condition, disappearance condition, non-disappearance condition: one [way].
Enumeration is based on cause.
The Section on Objects, etc.
(When established upon an object, there are always three questions in each case.)

With object condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya), there are three [results] with root condition (hetu), three with predominance condition (adhipati) …pe… three with non-disappearance condition (avigata) …pe….
With predominance condition (adhipati-paccaya), there are nine with root condition, three with object condition …pe… nine with non-disappearance condition …pe….
With proximity condition (anantara-paccaya) and contiguity condition (samanantara-paccaya), there are three with root condition …pe… three with non-disappearance condition …pe….
With co-nascence condition, nine [types] with root condition … pe … With mutuality condition,
three [types] with root condition … pe … With support condition,
nine [types] with root condition … pe …

With the condition of decisive support (upanissaya-paccaya), there are three [results] with respect to the root-cause (hetu) …pe… With the condition of prenascence (purejāta-paccaya), there are three [results] with respect to the root-cause …pe… The dyad of repetition (āsevana-duka).
By way of repetition-condition (āsevanapaccaya): three with root-cause (hetu), three with object (ārammaṇa), three with predominance (adhipati), three with proximity (anantara),

three with contiguity (samanantara), three with co-nascence (sahajāta), three with mutuality (aññamañña), three with dependence (nissaya), three with strong-dependence (upanissaya), three with prenascence (purejāta), three with kamma (kamma), three with nutriment (āhāra),
three with faculty (indriya), three with jhāna (jhāna), three with path (magga), three with association (sampayutta), [three] with dissociation (vippayutta).
Three for presence; three for absence; three for disappearance; three for non-disappearance. (In the section rooted in repetition, there is no resultant.
The Duality of Karma:
With kamma-condition and root-condition, there are nine... [and so on].
In the Vipākaduka, with resultant condition as the basis, there is one [condition] for root, one for object, one for predominance, one for proximity, one for contiguity,
one for conascence, one for mutuality, one for dependence, one for strong-dependence, and one for prenascence.

One with respect to kamma, one with respect to nutriment, one with respect to faculty, one with respect to jhāna, one with respect to path, one with respect to association, one with respect to dissociation, one with respect to presence, one with respect to absence, one with respect to disappearance, and one with respect to non-disappearance. (In the section based on resultant, there is no repetition.
[This concludes] the Nutriment-Duo and so forth.
With nutriment-condition, nine [types of consciousness] arise by way of root-cause …pe….
With faculty-condition, nine [types of consciousness] arise by way of root-cause …pe….
With jhāna-condition, nine [types of consciousness] arise by way of root-cause …pe….
With path-condition, nine [types] with root-condition …pe… With association-condition,
three [types] with root-condition …pe… With dissociation-condition,
nine [types] with root-condition …pe…
With presence condition, nine [answers] for root condition ... pe ...
With absence condition, three [answers] for root condition ... pe ...
With disappearance condition, three [answers] for root condition ... pe ...
In the Non-disappearance Dyad:
with non-disappearance condition, there are nine [answers] for root, three for object, nine for predominance …pe… three for absence, and three for disappearance.
These should be counted by one who is reciting after making each condition the basis.
Positive Order.
1.2.1.2. Negative Order of Conditions:
Section on Analysis.

Dependent on an unwholesome state, an unwholesome state arises by way of the not-root condition: dependent on the aggregates accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness, there arises delusion accompanied by doubt and accompanied by restlessness.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of the not-root condition: rootless resultant-indeterminate [states].
In dependence on one functional indeterminate aggregate, there arise three aggregates and mind-produced matter;
in dependence on three aggregates, there arise one aggregate and mind-produced matter; in dependence on two aggregates, there arise two aggregates and mind-produced matter;
and at the moment of rootless rebirth-linking, in dependence on one resultant indeterminate aggregate...
Three aggregates and the matter produced by kamma; one aggregate dependent on three aggregates and the matter produced by kamma;
two aggregates dependent on two aggregates and the matter produced by kamma; the bases dependent on the aggregates, and the aggregates dependent on the bases;
one great primary element dependent on three great primary elements, and three great primary elements dependent on one.
One great primary element in dependence on two great primary elements; two great primary elements in dependence on two great primary elements;
great primary elements in dependence on mind-originated matter, kamma-born matter, and derived matter; external [matter]... nutriment-originated matter... temperature-originated matter...
in the case of non-percipient beings, one great primary element in dependence on three great primary elements, and three great primary elements in dependence on one great primary element; two...
Dependent on great primaries, two great primaries [arise]; dependent on great primaries, kamma-produced matter and derived matter [arise].
By way of non-object condition:

A neutral (abyākata) state arises in dependence on a wholesome (kusala) state by way of mutual condition (aññamañña-paccaya): mind-produced matter arises in dependence on the wholesome aggregates.
A neutral state arises in dependence on an unwholesome (akusala) state by way of mutual condition: mind-produced matter arises in dependence on the unwholesome aggregates.
Dependent on an indeterminate state, an indeterminate state arises by way of not-mutuality condition:

Derived form: derived form dependent on external primary elements; derived form dependent on primary elements originated by nutriment;

Dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises not by way of mutuality condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great primaries, mind-produced matter arises.

Dependent on a wholesome state, a wholesome state arises by way of the not-prenascence condition: in the formless realm, one wholesome...

Dependent on one great primary element, there are three great primary elements; dependent on three great primary elements, there is one great primary element; dependent on two great primary elements, there are two great primary elements.

Form: dependent on one great primary element, three great primary elements arise … dependent on the great primary elements, mind-originated derived form arises;

Dependent on wholesome and indeterminate states, an indeterminate state arises by way of non-resultant condition: dependent on wholesome aggregates and the great primaries, mind-originated matter [arises].

external... nutriment-originated... temperature-originated... and in the case of non-percipient beings...
Dependent on one great primary element, three great primary elements arise … dependent on the great primary elements, kamma-produced derived matter arises.

(Non-absence and non-disappearance)

Dependent on a wholesome state, an indeterminate state arises by way of the condition of absence (*nonatthipaccaya*) … by way of the condition of disappearance (*novigatapaccaya*)—dependent on the wholesome aggregates, mind-produced matter [arises]. (This is the same as the non-object condition.

A wholesome and indeterminate state is related to a wholesome and indeterminate state by way of root condition:
wholesome roots are related to their associated aggregates and to mind-produced matter by way of root condition.
An unwholesome state is related to an unwholesome state by way of root condition: unwholesome roots are related to their associated [states]...
[Unwholesome states] are related to aggregates by way of root condition. An unwholesome state is related to an indeterminate state by way of root condition:
unwholesome roots are related to mind-produced matter by way of root condition.
An unwholesome state is related to both unwholesome and indeterminate states by way of root condition: unwholesome roots [are related] to their associated [states]...
The aggregates are a condition for mind-originated matter by way of root-condition.
An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of root-condition:
indeterminate resultant roots and indeterminate functional roots are a condition for their associated aggregates and for mind-originated matter by way of root-condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, resultant indeterminate roots are related to their associated aggregates and to the kamma-produced matter by way of the root condition.
Object...
A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of object-condition:
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, and performed the Uposatha duty, one reviews it; one reviews past deeds well done; having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna;
trainees review change-of-lineage (gotrabhū) and review purification (vodāna). Trainees...

Having emerged from the path, they review the path; or, whether they be trainees (*sekkha*) or worldlings (*puthujjana*), they practice insight into the wholesome as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
or, by means of the knowledge of others' minds (*cetopariyañāṇa*), they know the mind of one possessing a wholesome state of consciousness.

Wholesome [consciousness] pertaining to the base of infinite space is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for wholesome [consciousness] pertaining to the base of infinite consciousness. Wholesome [consciousness] pertaining to the base of nothingness...

The wholesome state of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related [to it] by way of object condition. Wholesome aggregates are related to the knowledge of the modes of psychic power,

the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds, and the knowledge of future existences, by way of object condition.
A wholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*):
having given a gift, undertaken virtue, and performed the observance-day duty (*uposathakamma*), one relishes it and delights in it;
taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, and grief arises. Previously...

One relishes and delights in well-performed deeds; based on that, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, and displeasure arises. Having emerged from jhāna, one relishes and delights in the jhāna;
based on that, lust arises, wrong view arises, and doubt arises.
Restlessness arises. When jhāna has been lost, remorse arises, and in one who is remorseful, mental grief arises.
A wholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of object-condition: an arahant, having emerged from the path, reviews the path;
he reviews past deeds well-performed; he reviews the wholesome as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.
One sees with insight; one knows the mind of one possessing a wholesome mind by means of the knowledge of penetration of others' minds.
Learners or worldlings see the wholesome as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; when the wholesome has ceased, its result arises as an object-condition (*tadārammaṇa*).
One relishes and delights in the wholesome; taking that as an object, lust arises, and wrong view arises.
Doubt arises, restlessness arises, and mental distress arises; when unwholesome states have ceased, their result arises as an object-condition (*tadārammaṇa*).

Wholesome consciousness of the base of infinite space is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the resultant and functional consciousness of the base of infinite consciousness. Wholesome consciousness of the base of nothingness [is a condition] for the resultant consciousness of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception...

And [it is] a condition for functional [states] by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*). Wholesome aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings according to their deeds, the knowledge of future existences, and for advertence by way of object-condition.
An unwholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of object-condition: one relishes and delights in lust.
Taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, and displeasure arises.
One relishes and delights in that wrong view; taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, and displeasure arises. Taking that doubt...
Taking restlessness as an object, doubt arises; wrong view arises; restlessness arises; mental distress arises.
Taking restlessness as an object, restlessness arises; wrong view arises; doubt arises; mental distress arises.
Taking mental distress as an object, mental distress arises; wrong view arises; doubt arises.
Restlessness arises.
An unwholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of object-condition:
trainees review defilements that have been abandoned, they review defilements that have been suppressed, and they know defilements previously practiced.
Whether they be trainees (sekkhā) or worldlings (puthujjana), when they practice insight (vipassanā) into the unwholesome as impermanent, suffering, and non-self,

they know the mind of one possessing an unwholesome mind by means of the knowledge of penetration of others' minds (cetopariyañāṇa). Unwholesome aggregates are related to the knowledge of penetration of others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives (pubbenivāsānussatiñāṇa), the knowledge of the destination according to deeds (yathākammupagañāṇa),
and the knowledge of future states (anāgataṁsañāṇa) by way of object-condition (ārammaṇapaccaya).
An unwholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of object-condition: an Arahant reviews abandoned defilements;
he knows previously practiced defilements; he practices insight into the unwholesome as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
he knows the mind of one possessing an unwholesome mind by means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds; or [it is so for] trainees or worldlings.
Or, when one contemplates the unwholesome as impermanent, suffering, and non-self, once the wholesome has ceased, the resultant arises with that as its object.
One relishes and delights in the unwholesome; taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, and mental grief arises. When the unwholesome has ceased...

The result arises as its object-condition (*tadārammaṇatā*). Unwholesome aggregates are related to knowledge of the minds of others, knowledge of recollection of past lives, knowledge of the destiny according to deeds, and knowledge of future existences, as well as to advertence, by way of the object-condition.
A neutral state is related to a neutral state by way of the object-condition: an Arahant reviews his fruition.
One reviews Nibbāna. Nibbāna is related to the adverting of the fruit by way of object-condition.

An Arahant contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; [he contemplates] the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical base … the resultant indeterminate and functional indeterminate aggregates.
One contemplates [the object] as impermanent, suffering, and non-self; one sees a form with the divine eye; one hears a sound with the divine ear-element;
one knows, by means of the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the mind of one possessing a resultant indeterminate or functional indeterminate mind.
A functional state of the base of infinite space is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a functional state of the base of infinite consciousness.
The functional state of the base of nothingness is a condition, by way of object-condition, for the functional state of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
The visible-object base is a condition, by way of object-condition, for eye-consciousness. The sound-base is a condition for ear-consciousness;
the odor-base is a condition for nose-consciousness; the taste-base is a condition for tongue-consciousness; the tangible-object base is a condition for body-consciousness.

It is a condition for body-consciousness by way of object-condition. Indeterminate aggregates are a condition for the knowledge of the modes of psychic power, the knowledge of penetration into others' minds, the knowledge of recollection of past lives, the knowledge of future existences, and for adverting by way of object-condition.
An indeterminate state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of object-condition: those in training review their fruition-attainment.
They review Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for change-of-lineage, purification, and the path by way of object-condition.
Learners or worldlings practice insight into the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
[they do so] with respect to the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangibles … the physical basis [of consciousness].

They practice insight into the aggregates that are indeterminate as resultants (*vipākābyākata*) and indeterminate as functional (*kiriyābyākata*)—viewing them as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.

They see forms with the divine eye, hear sounds with the divine ear-element, and know with the knowledge of penetration of minds the mind of one possessing a resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate mind.

Indeterminate aggregates are the object of the knowledge of the various supernormal powers (*iddhividha-ñāṇa*), the knowledge of penetration of minds (*cetopariya-ñāṇa*), and the knowledge of recollection of past lives (*pubbenivāsānussati-ñāṇa*).
It is a condition for the knowledge of future states by way of object-condition.
An indeterminate state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of object-condition: one relishes and delights in the eye;
with that as object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, and restlessness arises.

Mental distress arises. [One] delights in and rejoices over the ear… the nose… the tongue… the body… forms… sounds… odors… tastes… tangibles… the physical basis [of consciousness]… and the resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregates;
taking that as an object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, and restlessness arises.
Mental distress arises.
A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of predominance-condition: as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance.
Object-predominance: Having given a gift, undertaken virtue, or performed the uposatha duties, one reviews that with esteem;
one reviews past well-performed deeds with esteem; having emerged from jhāna, one reviews the jhāna with esteem.
Learners (sekkhā) review change-of-lineage (gotrabhu) with esteem; they review purification (vodāna) with esteem...
[They] reflect upon it after having made [it an object]. Learners (sekkhā), having emerged from the path, reflect upon the path, esteeming it as venerable.
Co-nascent predominance (sahajātādhipati): wholesome predominance is a condition for its associated aggregates by way of the predominance condition.
A wholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of the predominance condition. Object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati): [such as] giving...
Having given a gift, undertaken precepts, and performed the Uposatha observance, one esteems, relishes, and delights in that;
esteeming it, lust arises and wrong view arises. Esteeming previously well-performed deeds, one esteems, relishes, and delights in them;
esteeming them, lust arises and wrong view arises. Having emerged from jhāna...
Taking jhāna as an object, one esteems it and delights in it; taking that as an object, lust arises and wrong view arises.
A wholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of predominance-condition (adhipati-paccaya):

namely, object-predominance (ārammaṇādhipati) and co-nascent predominance (sahajātādhipati). Object-predominance: an Arahant, having emerged from the path, esteems and reviews the path. Co-nascent predominance: wholesome predominance.
It is a condition for mind-originated material phenomena by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
A wholesome state is a condition for both wholesome and indeterminate states by way of the predominance condition. As co-nascent predominance (*sahajātādhipati*):
wholesome predominance is a condition for its associated aggregates and mind-originated material phenomena by way of the predominance condition.

An unwholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of predominance-condition (*adhipatipaccaya*): as object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*) and as conascence-predominance (*sahajātādhipati*).
As object-predominance: one esteems, relishes, and delights in lust (*rāga*);
esteeming it, lust arises and wrong view (*diṭṭhi*) arises. One esteems, relishes, and delights in wrong view; esteeming it, lust [arises].
[Wrong] view arises. Conascence-predominance: unwholesome predominance is related to its associated aggregates by way of predominance condition.

An unwholesome state is related to an indeterminate state by way of predominance condition. Conascence-predominance: unwholesome predominance is related to mind-produced matter by way of predominance condition.
An unwholesome state is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for both unwholesome and indeterminate states.
As co-nascent predominance: an unwholesome predominance is a condition, by way of predominance condition, for the associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of predominance-condition:
as object-predominance and as conascence-predominance. Object-predominance: an Arahant, esteeming the fruit, reviews it;

esteeming Nibbāna, he reviews it. Nibbāna is a condition for the fruit by way of predominance-condition. Conascence-predominance: predominance of resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate states.
It is a condition for its associated aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of the predominance condition (*adhipatipaccaya*).
An indeterminate state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the predominance condition. As object-predominance (*ārammaṇādhipati*):
trainees esteem and review the fruit; they esteem and review Nibbāna. Nibbāna...
The state of lineage, purification, and the path are related to [their respective subsequent states] by way of predominance condition.
An indeterminate state is related to an unwholesome state by way of predominance condition. As object-predominance:
one esteems the eye, relishes it, and delights in it; esteeming it, lust arises and wrong view arises.

One esteems, relishes, and delights in the ear... the nose... the tongue... the body... visible forms... sounds... odors... tastes... tangibles... the physical base... and the resultant indeterminate or functional indeterminate aggregates.
Esteeming them, lust arises; wrong view arises.
A preceding wholesome state is a condition for a subsequent wholesome state by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
Preceding wholesome aggregates are a condition for subsequent wholesome aggregates by way of proximity-condition. Adaptation (*anuloma*).

The state of lineage is related to conformity by way of proximity condition; conformity is related to purification by way of proximity condition; the state of lineage is related to the path by way of proximity condition; purification is related to the path by way of proximity condition.
A wholesome state is related to an indeterminate state by way of proximity condition: wholesome [consciousness] is related to emergence; the path is related to the fruit;

conformity is related to the attainment of the fruit of a trainee; for one emerging from cessation, the wholesome [consciousness] of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related [to the subsequent state].
It is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).

An unwholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of proximity-condition: preceding unwholesome aggregates are a condition for succeeding unwholesome aggregates by way of proximity-condition.
An unwholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of proximity-condition: the unwholesome [state] is a condition for emergence (*vuṭṭhāna*) by way of proximity-condition.
An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*):
preceding resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregates are a condition for subsequent resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregates by way of proximity condition;
the life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) for the adverting consciousness (*āvajjanā*); functional consciousness for emergence (*vuṭṭhāna*); and the conformity [consciousness] of an Arahant.

For one emerging from the attainment of fruition or from cessation, the functional state of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
An indeterminate state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of proximity-condition: adverting is a condition for the wholesome aggregates by way of proximity-condition.
An indeterminate state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of proximity-condition: advertence is a condition for unwholesome aggregates by way of proximity-condition.
Immediate:
A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of immediate-condition: preceding wholesome [states]...
The preceding aggregates are a condition for the succeeding wholesome aggregates by way of proximity-condition (*samanantara-paccaya*).

Adaptation is a condition for change-of-lineage; adaptation is a condition for purification; change-of-lineage is a condition for the Path; and purification is a condition for the Path by way of proximity-condition.
A wholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the immediately preceding condition (*samanantara-paccaya*): wholesome [consciousness] for emergence;

the Path for the Fruit; conformity for the attainment of the fruit of a trainee; and for one emerging from cessation, wholesome consciousness of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the attainment of the fruit by way of the immediately preceding condition.

An unwholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of the immediately preceding condition: preceding unwholesome aggregates are a condition for succeeding unwholesome aggregates by way of the immediately preceding condition.

An unwholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the immediately preceding condition: the unwholesome [state] is a condition for emergence by way of the immediately preceding condition.
An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the immediately preceding condition: preceding [indeterminate states]...

Resultant indeterminate and functional indeterminate aggregates are related to subsequent resultant indeterminate and functional indeterminate aggregates by way of proximity condition (*samanantara-paccaya*).
The life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) is related to the adverting consciousness; functional consciousness is related to emergence;

for an Arahant, conformity is related to the attainment of fruition; and for one emerging from cessation, the functional consciousness of the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is related [to the subsequent consciousness].
The attainment of fruition is related to [itself] by way of the condition of immediate proximity.
An indeterminate state is related to a wholesome state by way of the condition of immediate proximity: advertence is related to wholesome aggregates by way of the condition of immediate proximity.

An indeterminate state is related to an unwholesome state by way of the condition of immediate proximity: advertence is related to unwholesome aggregates by way of the condition of immediate proximity.
A co-nascent wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the co-nascence condition: one wholesome aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of the co-nascence condition;
three aggregates are a condition for one aggregate by way of the co-nascence condition.
Condition. Two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates by way of co-nascence condition (*sahajāta-paccaya*).
A wholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition: wholesome aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
A wholesome state is a condition for both wholesome and indeterminate states by way of co-nascence condition: the wholesome...
One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
Three aggregates are a condition for one aggregate and for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
Two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
An unwholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of co-nascence condition:
one unwholesome aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of co-nascence condition; three aggregates are a condition for one aggregate by way of co-nascence condition;
two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates by way of co-nascence condition.
An unwholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition: unwholesome aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
An unwholesome state is a condition for both an unwholesome and an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition:
one unwholesome aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
Three aggregates are a condition for one aggregate and for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
Two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition: namely, resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate [states].
One aggregate is a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
Three aggregates are a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for one aggregate and for mind-produced matter.
Two aggregates are a condition, by way of co-nascence condition, for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, one resultant indeterminate aggregate is a conascence condition for three aggregates and for the [kamma-]born material phenomena.
Three aggregates are a conascence condition for one aggregate and for the [kamma-]born material phenomena.
Two aggregates are a conascence condition for two aggregates and for the [kamma-]born material phenomena.
The aggregates are related to the physical basis by way of the co-nascence condition; the physical basis is related to the aggregates by way of the co-nascence condition.

One great primary element is related to three great primary elements by way of the co-nascence condition; three great primary elements are related to one great primary element by way of the co-nascence condition;
two great primary elements are related to two great primary elements [by way of the co-nascence condition].
It is a condition by way of co-nascence condition. The great primary elements are a condition by way of co-nascence condition for mind-produced matter, kamma-produced matter, and derived matter.
One external great primary element is a condition by way of co-nascence condition for three great primary elements;
three great primary elements are a condition by way of co-nascence condition for one great primary element; two great primary elements... [are a condition] for two great primary elements.
Two great elements are related to [the other] two great elements by way of co-nascence condition. Great elements are related to derived matter by way of co-nascence condition.
One great element produced by nutriment is related to three great elements by way of co-nascence condition.
Three great elements are related to one great element by way of co-nascence condition. Two great elements...

Two great primary elements (mahābhūta) are related to [the other] two great primary elements by way of co-nascence condition (sahajātapaccaya). Great primary elements are related to derived matter (upādārūpa) by way of co-nascence condition.
One temperature-originated (utusamuṭṭhāna) great primary element is related to three great primary elements by way of co-nascence condition.
Three great primary elements are related to one great primary element by way of co-nascence condition. Two great primary elements...

Two great elements are a condition for [the others] by way of the co-nascent condition (*sahajātapaccaya*). Great elements are a condition for derived matter (*upādārūpa*) by way of the co-nascent condition.
For non-percipient beings (*asaññasatta*), one great element is a condition for three great elements by way of the co-nascent condition;
three great elements are a condition for one great element by way of the co-nascent condition; two great elements...

Two great elements are related to [other] great elements by way of co-nascence condition. Great elements are related to both the matter produced by kamma (*kaṭattā-rūpa*) and derived matter (*upādāya-rūpa*) by way of co-nascence condition.

Wholesome and indeterminate states are related to an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition: wholesome aggregates and great elements are related to mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.

Unwholesome and indeterminate states are related to an indeterminate state by way of co-nascence condition: unwholesome aggregates and great primaries are related to mind-produced matter by way of co-nascence condition.
Mutuality Condition:
A wholesome state is related to a wholesome state by way of mutuality condition: one wholesome aggregate is related to three [aggregates]... [and so on].
The aggregates are related to one another by way of mutual condition (*aññamañña-paccaya*). Three aggregates are related to one aggregate by way of mutual condition;
two aggregates are related to two aggregates by way of mutual condition.
An unwholesome state is related to an unwholesome state by way of mutual condition: one unwholesome aggregate [is related to the other three].
Three aggregates are related to one another by way of mutuality condition. Three aggregates are related to one aggregate by way of mutuality condition.
Two aggregates are related to two aggregates by way of mutuality condition.
An indeterminate state is related to an indeterminate state by way of mutuality condition: namely, resultant-indeterminate and functional-indeterminate states.
One aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of mutuality condition; three aggregates are a condition for one aggregate by way of mutuality condition;
two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates by way of mutuality condition.
At the moment of rebirth-linking, a resultant indeterminate aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and for the physical basis...
And [they are] a condition by way of mutuality-condition. Three aggregates are a condition by way of mutuality-condition for one aggregate and the physical basis.
Two aggregates are a condition by way of mutuality-condition for two aggregates and the physical basis.
The aggregates are a condition by way of mutuality-condition for the physical basis; the physical basis is a condition by way of mutuality-condition for the aggregates.
Condition: One great primary element is a condition for three great primary elements by way of mutuality condition.

Three great primary elements are a condition for one great primary element by way of mutuality condition. Two great primary elements are a condition for two great primary elements by way of mutuality condition;
likewise for external [elements], those produced by nutriment, those produced by temperature, and those of non-percipient beings.

One great primary element is a condition for three great primary elements by way of mutuality-condition …pe… two great primary elements are conditions for two great primary elements by way of mutuality-condition.
(Dependence)
A wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of the support-condition (nissaya-paccaya): one wholesome aggregate is a condition for three aggregates by way of the support-condition;
three aggregates are a condition for one aggregate by way of the support-condition;
two aggregates are a condition for two aggregates by way of the support-condition.
A wholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of dependence condition: wholesome aggregates are a condition for mind-produced matter by way of dependence condition.
A wholesome state is a condition for both wholesome and indeterminate states by way of dependence condition:
one wholesome aggregate is a condition for three aggregates and mind-produced matter by way of dependence condition.

Three aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for one aggregate and for mind-produced matter. Two aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter. An unwholesome state is a condition, by way of support-condition, for an unwholesome state: one unwholesome aggregate... [is a condition] for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter. Three aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for one aggregate and for mind-produced matter. Two aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter. An unwholesome state is a condition, by way of support-condition, for an unwholesome state: one unwholesome aggregate... [is a condition] for another unwholesome aggregate. An unwholesome state is a condition, by way of support-condition, for an indeterminate state: unwholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for mind-produced matter. Unwholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for kamma-produced matter. Unwholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for great primary elements. Great primary elements are a condition, by way of support-condition, for derived matter. One unwholesome aggregate is a condition, by way of support-condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter. Three aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for one aggregate and for mind-produced matter. Two aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter. An unwholesome state is a condition, by way of support-condition, for an unwholesome state: one unwholesome aggregate... [is a condition] for another unwholesome aggregate. An unwholesome state is a condition, by way of support-condition, for an indeterminate state: unwholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for mind-produced matter. Unwholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for kamma-produced matter. Unwholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for great primary elements. Great primary elements are a condition, by way of support-condition, for derived matter. One unwholesome aggregate is a condition, by way of support-condition, for three aggregates and for mind-produced matter. Three aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for one aggregate and for mind-produced matter. Two aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for two aggregates and for mind-produced matter. An unwholesome state is a condition, by way of support-condition, for an unwholesome state: one unwholesome aggregate... [is a condition] for another unwholesome aggregate. An unwholesome state is a condition, by way of support-condition, for an indeterminate state: unwholesome aggregates are a condition, by way of support-condition, for mind-produced matter. The act of matricide is a condition for the act of matricide by way of decisive support condition. The act of matricide...

An unwholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of decisive support condition. Natural decisive support: lust … [and so on].
