An unwholesome state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of decisive support condition (upanissaya-paccaya)—namely, as immediate decisive support (anantara-upanissaya) and natural decisive support (pakata-upanissaya).
Proximity-predominance condition (*anantara-rūpa-nissaya*): Unwholesome states are a condition for emergence by way of the predominance condition.
Natural-predominance condition (*pakata-upanissaya*): Relying on lust, one torments oneself and causes oneself to suffer;
one experiences suffering rooted in searching. [Likewise] relying on hatred … delusion … conceit … wrong view … aspiration … [one acts].
One torments oneself, makes oneself suffer, and experiences suffering rooted in searching.
Greed, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, and aspiration are related to bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).
Unwholesome kamma is related to its result by way of decisive support condition.

An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*): as object-decisive support, proximity-decisive support, and natural decisive support.

Object-decisive support: An Arahant, esteeming it, reviews the fruit; esteeming it, he reviews Nibbāna. Nibbāna is a condition for the fruit by way of decisive support condition. Proximity-decisive support:
Preceding resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregates are [conditions] for succeeding [aggregates].
It is a condition, by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*), for subsequent resultant indeterminate aggregates and functional indeterminate aggregates.
The life-continuum (*bhavaṅga*) is a condition for adverting; functional [consciousness] for emergence; for an Arahant, conformity is a condition for the attainment of fruition;

and for one emerging from cessation, the functional consciousness of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception is a condition for the attainment of fruition, by way of decisive support condition.

Natural strong-dependence (*pakatūpanissaya*): Bodily pleasure is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and the attainment of fruition (*phalasamāpatti*) by way of the condition of strong-dependence.

Bodily pain is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and the attainment of fruition by way of the condition of strong-dependence. Temperature (*utu*) [is a condition] for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, ...

It is a condition for the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). Food is a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition.
Lodgings are a condition for bodily pleasure, bodily pain, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition. Bodily pleasure...

… Bodily suffering … temperature … food … and lodging are related to bodily pleasure, bodily suffering, and the attainment of fruition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). The attainment of fruition is related to bodily pleasure by way of decisive support condition.
An Arahant, relying on bodily pleasure, generates an unarisen functional attainment (*kiriyā-samāpatti*) and enters an arisen one.
He contemplates volitional formations as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. Depending on bodily pain, temperature, food, or lodging,
he generates an unarisen functional attainment (*kiriyasamāpatti*),
enters an arisen one, and contemplates volitional formations as impermanent, suffering, and non-self.

An indeterminate state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*): as object-decisive support, as proximity-decisive support, and as natural-decisive support.

As object-decisive support: trainees (*sekha*) hold the fruit in high esteem and review it; they hold Nibbāna in high esteem and review it. Nibbāna is a condition for the change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*), for purification (*vodāna*), and for the path by way of decisive support condition.
As proximity-decisive support: adverting [consciousness] is a condition for the wholesome aggregates by way of decisive support condition.

Natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*): Relying on bodily happiness, one gives a gift, undertakes virtue, performs the Uposatha observance, arouses jhāna, arouses insight, arouses the Path, arouses direct knowledge (*abhiññā*), and arouses meditative attainment (*samāpatti*).
[Likewise] relying on bodily pain, temperature, food, and lodging, one gives a gift...
One gives; one undertakes virtue; one performs the Uposatha observance; one arouses jhāna; one arouses insight;
one arouses the path; one arouses direct knowledge; one arouses meditative attainment.
Bodily pleasure… bodily pain… climate… food… lodging… faith… virtue… learning… generosity… wisdom.
Condition by way of decisive support condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*).

An indeterminate state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of decisive support condition—namely, object-decisive support (*ārammaṇūpanissaya*), proximity-decisive support (*anantarūpanissaya*), and natural decisive support (*pakatūpanissaya*).
As object-decisive support: one esteems the eye, relishes it, and delights in it; esteeming it, lust [arises].
...view arises. [Regarding] the ear ... the nose ... the tongue ... the body ... visible forms ...

sounds ... odors ... tastes ... tangibles ... the physical basis ... having taken the resultant indeterminate or functional indeterminate aggregates as an object of esteem, one relishes them and delights in them; taking them as an object of esteem, lust arises and view arises.
Proximity-decadence condition (*anantarūpanissaya*): Advertence is a condition for unwholesome aggregates by way of the decisive support condition (*upanissayapaccaya*).

Natural-decadence condition (*pakatūpanissaya*): Relying on bodily pleasure, one kills a living being, takes what is not given, speaks falsehood, speaks maliciously, speaks harshly, indulges in idle chatter, breaks into a dwelling, or carries off plunder.
He commits burglary; he stands as an ambusher; he commits adultery; he commits plundering of a village; he commits plundering of a town;
he deprives his mother of life; he deprives his father of life;
he deprives an arahant of life; with a malicious mind, he draws blood from a Tathāgata; he causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Physical suffering … [and so on] … temperature … food … depending on a lodging, one takes life … [abbreviated]. One causes a schism in the Saṅgha.
Physical pleasure … physical suffering … temperature … food … a lodging is a condition by way of decisive support for lust, hatred, delusion, conceit, wrong view, and longing.
Pre-nascence.
An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of prenascence condition—namely, object-prenascence and base-prenascence.
Regarding object-prenascence: an Arahant contemplates the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
[likewise] the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangible objects.
...pe... one contemplates the physical basis as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;
one sees a visible form with the divine eye; one hears a sound with the divine ear-element. The base of visible forms is a condition for eye-consciousness by way of prenascence-condition.
The base of sounds is a condition for ear-consciousness ...pe... the base of odors is a condition for nose-consciousness ...pe... the base of tastes is a condition for tongue-consciousness ...pe...
The sphere of tangible objects is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-arising condition.
As for the pre-arising of the physical basis: the eye-sphere is a condition for eye-consciousness by way of pre-arising condition;
the ear-sphere for ear-consciousness … the nose-sphere for nose-consciousness … the tongue-sphere for tongue-consciousness … [and so on].

…pe… The body-base is a condition for body-consciousness by way of pre-arising condition. The physical basis (vatthu) is a condition for resultant indeterminate and functional indeterminate aggregates by way of pre-arising condition.
An indeterminate state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of pre-arising condition: namely, object-pre-arising and base-pre-arising.
Object-prenascence: Learners or worldlings practice insight into the eye as impermanent, suffering, and non-self;

[they practice insight] into the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … odors … tastes … tangible objects … and into the [heart-]base as impermanent, suffering, and non-self. With the divine eye...
They see forms. With the divine ear-element, they hear sounds.
Base-prenascence: the base is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for wholesome aggregates.
An indeterminate state is a condition, by way of prenascence-condition, for an unwholesome state: namely, object-prenascence.
Base-prenascence. Object-prenascence: one relishes and delights in the eye;
with that as object, lust arises, wrong view arises, doubt arises, restlessness arises, and grief arises.
[The same applies to] the ear … the nose … the tongue … the body … visible forms … sounds … smells … [tastes … tangible objects].
... pe ... tastes ... pe ... tangibles ... pe ... one relishes and delights in the physical basis (vatthu). Taking that as an object, lust arises ...
pe ... grief arises. Basis-prenascence:
the physical basis is a condition for unwholesome aggregates by way of the prenascence condition.
A wholesome state is related to an indeterminate state by way of postnascence condition: postnascent wholesome aggregates are related to this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.
An unwholesome state is related to an indeterminate state by way of postnascence condition: postnascent unwholesome aggregates are related to this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.

An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of postnascence condition: postnascent resultant-indeterminate or functional-indeterminate aggregates are a condition for this prenascent body by way of postnascence condition.
Regarding repetition:
a wholesome state is a condition for a wholesome state by way of repetition condition: preceding wholesome aggregates [are a condition for succeeding ones].
Each preceding wholesome aggregate is a condition for each subsequent wholesome aggregate by way of the condition of repetition (*āsevanapaccaya*).

Adaptation (*anuloma*) is a condition for change-of-lineage (*gotrabhū*), adaptation is a condition for purification (*vodāna*), change-of-lineage is a condition for the Path (*magga*), and purification is a condition for the Path by way of the condition of repetition.

An unwholesome state is a condition for an unwholesome state by way of the condition of repetition: each preceding unwholesome aggregate is a condition for each subsequent unwholesome aggregate by way of the condition of repetition.

An indeterminate state is a condition for an indeterminate state by way of the condition of repetition (āsevana-paccaya): preceding functional-indeterminate aggregates are a condition for succeeding functional-indeterminate aggregates by way of the condition of repetition.
